# CH. Clicker: working rules (dev-flow)

Permanent rules for AI coding agents working on this repository. They are not suggestions: follow them exactly.

## 1. Continuous phases (authorized by the user on 2026-10-04)

The user authorized running the phases in sequence without pausing between them; they interrupt if they notice something. Every phase still closes completely:
implement → verify → 10-layer review → fix → update `refs/` → commit → short report → next phase.
Trade-off decisions (cost, security, scope changes) still go to the user before moving on. If a session is interrupted mid-phase, resume the same phase.

## 2. Commits

- Format: Conventional Commits (`feat:`, `fix:`, `chore:`, `test:`, `docs:`, `refactor:`), with the phase scope when useful (`feat(engine): ...`).
- Granularity: one commit per phase, with a bulleted body explaining what and why, plus any accepted limitations.
- Message language: English (open-source project; decided by the user on 2026-10-05).
- Branches: straight to `main` (solo project). Remote: `github.com/chenoli/chenoli-auto-clicker`.
- Never push, open a PR, `--amend` or `--no-verify` without an explicit request.

## 3. 10-layer review + lint --fix

Before declaring any phase done, review and actually check (`npm view`, `pnpm ls`, `pnpm audit`, `cargo tree`, `grep`/`find`):
architecture · security · dependencies · data (here: on-disk persistence and JSON schema) · quality/TypeScript/Rust · conventions · build/tooling · infra (here: installer, signing, CI) · tests · documentation/DX.
Run `pnpm lint:fix`, `pnpm format` and `cargo fmt --all` as part of the review. A phase closes with zero warnings (`eslint --max-warnings 0`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`).

## 4. Project

- Repo shape: single app. Cargo workspace (`crates/*` + `src-tauri`) and a pnpm frontend in `ui/`.
- Stack: Tauri 2 + Rust (`windows-rs`) in the core; React 19 + TypeScript 6 + Vite 8 + Tailwind v4 in the UI. Full architecture in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`; backlog in `docs/TASKS.md`.
- Design system: high-fidelity handoff in `refs/` (`refs/README.md`, `refs/design/CH Clicker.dc.html`). Tokens versioned in `design/tokens.json` (source of truth; `pnpm tokens` generates `themes.css`, `tokens.ts` and `tokens.rs`). Read the screen spec in the handoff README before building a screen.
- Languages: conversation with the user and `refs/` in Brazilian Portuguese; commits, public documentation (`README`, `docs/`, community files in `.github/`), internal error messages and code identifiers in English; UI i18n: pt-BR, en-US and es-419 (i18next, typed keys).

## 5. Code conventions

- File names: kebab-case, enforced by lint (`eslint-plugin-check-file`). Rust uses snake_case.
- Formatting: Prettier (double quotes, semicolons, 120 columns); `rustfmt` for Rust.
- Comments: none in code (no doc comments, none in generated files). The only exception: `unsafe` blocks always carry `// SAFETY:` (required by clippy's `undocumented_unsafe_blocks`).
- Lint: strict. `react-hooks` as errors, no `any`, no `console` outside `tools/` and `ui/tests/`, separate `import type`, enforced import order (perfectionist). Clippy with `-D warnings`.
- Import order: side effects → react → external → app contexts (`components`, `dev`, `features`, `i18n`, `ipc`, `store`, `styles`) → relative → `import type` last.
- Design tokens: never arbitrary Tailwind values (`text-[12px]`). Colors come from `design/tokens.json`; the type scale and tracking live in the `@theme` of `ui/src/styles/base.css`. One-off mixes from the handoff use a local `color-mix()`, without creating a new token name.

## 6. Tests and verification

- A co-located test for all new code, in the same phase. Minimum 80% coverage for lines, branches, functions and statements (breaks the pipeline): Vitest in the frontend; `cargo llvm-cov` for the crates with logic.
- Screens: verify in the real Tauri window and in the gallery (`ui/gallery.html`), in the Grafite (dark) and Papel (light) themes, with the screenshot opened and checked; prototype parity through Playwright.
- **Real input (clicks, moves, hotkeys):** tests that inject system input are `#[ignore]`. The user often has games open on screen 2 (`DISPLAY2`): real input only on screen 1 (`DISPLAY1`, primary), with `CH_TEST_MONITORS=primary`. Never move the cursor, click or open windows on screen 2. Before any real click, drag or move, confirm the window under the point belongs to the `ch-clicker` process (screen 1 may have games open too); engine runs that move the cursor need the same check for the whole area.
- Timing benchmarks (`tools/jitter-bench`) record their results in `docs/bench/`.

## 7. Security

- The emergency stop can never be disabled or blocked (ARCHITECTURE §10.1).
- The app never clicks its own window and does not hide its activity (events marked as injected).
- File inputs (`.chprofile` import) are validated by content and schema, never by what the file claims.
- Code signing and the updater depend on real secrets (see `docs/release.md`); the updater private key is never committed.

## 8. Task management

- Tracker: only the local backlog (`docs/TASKS.md`, versioned) and progress in `refs/architecture/plano-tarefas.md`.
- Writing to an external tracker: not applicable.
- `/dev-flow:feature <description>` starts a feature outside the backlog; its plan lives in `refs/features/`.

## 9. References

- `refs/` (outside git): design handoff, `architecture/plano-tarefas.md` (phase progress), `features/`, `third-party/`. Index in `refs/INDEX.md`.
- Update the progress file every phase, even though it is not versioned. The official history is `git log`.
